implied_return.note: The yearly return a buyer at today's price earns if each model's assumptions hold (an implied cost of capital). Above the cost of equity: the price leaves room; below: the price already asks for more than the models deliver.

wacc.formula: WACC = wₑ × kₑ + w_d × k_d × (1 − t);  kₑ = r_f + β × ERP
steps: β (Blume-adjusted) = 0.67 × raw β 0.28 + 0.33 = 0.52  (104 weekly returns vs SPY, R² 0.07)
k_d = 5.59%  (5-year Treasury 4.91% + model spread 68 bp (bond-calibrated, app/debt.py)); after tax 5.59% × (1 − 21%) = 4.42%

methods.formula: 10-year Monte Carlo: revenue growth switches between high / steady / decline regimes by a Markov chain; margin drifts by regime; value = Σ discounted FCFF − SBC + terminal, per share
assumptions: its own history + the panel prior (markov.json)
methods.fit: It has a DCF and enough quarters of revenue history to estimate how often its growth switches regime.

methods.formula: FCFF = EBIT × (1 − t) + D&A − capex − ΔWC;  EV = Σ FCFF/(1+WACC)^t + TV/(1+WACC)^5;  TV = NOPAT₆ × (1 − g ÷ ROIC) ÷ (WACC − g);  value = (EV − debt + cash − claims) ÷ shares
steps: growth by year 6%, 6%, 5%, 4%, 3%; EBIT margin 46.2%; D&A 1.7% of revenue; capex 12.9%, 11.5%, 10.1%, 8.7%, 7.3% of revenue; ΔWC 10% of each revenue increase
Monte Carlo: 2,000 scenarios, 10th–90th percentile $172.11 – $400.68; P(value > price) = 52%

methods.formula: Value = EPS × (8.5 + 2g) × 4.4 ÷ Y;  g = expected yearly growth in percent, Y = the AAA corporate yield today
inputs: FRED DAAA (via the Debt & rates module)
assumptions: the P/E of a company that does not grow
the AAA yield when Graham set the formula
an assumption: the formula overstates value at high growth
methods.fit: It has positive earnings and a growth estimate; the formula prices that growth against today's AAA bond yield.

methods.formula: Fair P/E = growth + dividend yield, in percent (5–40);  value = EPS × fair P/E;  PEGY = P/E ÷ (growth + yield)
steps: growth 6.7% (analysts' next-year EPS growth (32 analysts)); dividend yield 2.9%
today P/E 20.2 → PEGY 2.12 (below 1: cheap for its growth, above 2: dear)
assumptions: Peter Lynch, One Up on Wall Street (1989)
a rule of thumb, not a model of cash flows
analysts look one or two years ahead; Lynch meant several
methods.fit: It has positive earnings and a growth rate, so its P/E can be set against the growth and yield it delivers.

methods.formula: EPV = adjusted earnings ÷ WACC − net debt;  adjusted earnings = normalized EBIT × (1 − t) + D&A − maintenance capex;  normalized EBIT = average margin × revenue
steps: normalized EBIT = 46.2% × $27.70B = $12.80B  (the last four quarters' EBIT margin (fewer than three years on file))
maintenance capex = $1.89B  (capex $3.58B − growth capex (PP&E $28.48B ÷ revenue × revenue gain $1.64B = $1.69B))

methods.formula: Value = D₀ × [(1 + g_L) + H × (g_S − g_L)] ÷ (kₑ − g_L);  growth falls in a straight line from g_S to g_L over 2H years
